mainTopic: Bava Kamma 108b: who gets the thief's כפל, a thief's admission to the שומר or the owners, a שומר's duties once the thief is known, and a new משנה on false oaths about deposits.
overview: This amud deals with a שומר whose deposit was stolen, and with who gets the thief's כפל (double payment). It opens with the end of the argument between אביי and רבא about a שומר who both swore and paid. אביי says the oath decides, so the כפל goes to the owner. רבא says the payment decides, so it goes to the שומר. Each one rereads the משנה's clauses to fit his view. Next comes a case where the thief admits to the שומר. רבא rules that the admission frees the thief from כפל only if the שומר's oath was true, and his follow-up questions about false oaths end in תיקו. The reverse case, where the thief admits to owners who were already paid, also ends in תיקו. אביי and רבא then argue over whether a שומר חנם may swear his way out once the thief is known. A question from רבה זוטי about a stolen animal that the thief brought back also ends in תיקו. The amud closes with a new משנה about a שומר who swears falsely, a son who robbed his father, and a father's קונם against his son.

steps.title: אביי completes his reading of the first clause
steps.stepSummary: אביי infers from the רישא that once the שומר swore, the כפל goes to the owner even if he later paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he swore, even though he paid, to whom does the thief pay? To the owner of the deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes אביי's reading of the רישא. In his view, once the שומר swore, he loses the right to the כפל, even if he paid afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'he paid and did not want to swear.' אביי reads the words 'did not want to swear' as the key point. So if he did swear, paying later does not help him, and the כפל goes to the owner.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion starting here. It is the end of אביי's inference, which began just before this line on the דף.

steps.title: רבא infers the opposite from the last clause

steps.simpleTranslation: רבא inferred from the latter clause: 'He swore and did not want to pay.' The reason is that he did not want to pay. But if he paid, even though he swore, to whom does the thief pay? To the one who had the deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes the same kind of inference as אביי, but from the סיפא. He reaches the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא says 'he swore and did not want to pay.' רבא reads 'did not want to pay' as the key point. So if he did pay, even after swearing, the כפל goes to the שומר.

steps.title: The last clause is a problem for אביי

steps.simpleTranslation: According to אביי, the latter clause is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the סיפא, read רבא's way, contradicts אביי. This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the סיפא shows that paying gets the שומר the כפל even after an oath, then אביי's view, that the oath decides, clashes with the משנה itself.

steps.title: אביי rereads the last clause
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'did not want to pay' means he did not want to pay before the oath, only after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי could say to you: This is what it teaches. He swore, and did not want to pay before the oath, but only after the oath. To whom does the thief pay? To the owner of the deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. He reads the סיפא as describing a שומר who paid only after swearing, and in that case the כפל goes to the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's reading, 'did not want to pay' means 'did not want to pay before swearing.' So the סיפא is exactly the case of swearing and then paying, and it gives the כפל to the owner. That supports אביי instead of challenging him.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is teaching; a rereading of the text

steps.title: The first clause is a problem for רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי's reading of the רישא seems to go against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא, the first clause is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the other side. The רישא, read אביי's way, contradicts רבא, and רבא will answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא seemed to show that a שומר who swore loses the כפל even if he paid later. That clashes with רבא's view that payment decides.

steps.title: רבא rereads the first clause
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'did not want to swear' means he swore, did not want to stand by his oath, and paid instead.

steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's reading, 'did not want to swear' means 'did not want to stand by the oath he already took.' So the רישא is the case of swearing and then paying, and it gives the כפל to the שומר. That supports רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: To stand by his oath

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: once the שומר swears, the כפל goes to the owner, even if he pays later. רבא: once the שומר pays, the כפל goes to him, even if he swore first. Each one rereads the clause that seems to go against him so that it fits his view.

phrases.english: רבא could say to you: This is what it teaches:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבא, mirroring אביי's answer in step 4.

steps.title: New question: does admitting to the guardian free the thief?
steps.stepSummary: The שומר swore, and then the thief admitted to the שומר but denied to the owner, who brought witnesses. Is the thief now exempt from כפל?
steps.simpleTranslation: The owners demanded from the guardian, and he swore, and the thief was identified. The guardian demanded from the thief, and he admitted. Then the owners demanded from him, and he denied, and they brought witnesses. Is the thief exempt because he admitted to the guardian, or is he not exempt because he admitted to the guardian?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question with a step-by-step case. It asks whether the thief's admission to the שומר counts to free him from כפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, someone who admits to a קנס before witnesses come is exempt from it, and כפל is a קנס. But this שומר swore, so he no longer seems to have a claim against the thief. The question is whether admitting to a שומר who swore is a real admission that exempts the thief.

keyTerms.meaning: They demanded from him; made a claim against him
The thief was identified
He denied

Became exempt
One who admits to a fine is exempt from it

steps.whyThisMatters: This question tests whether a שומר who swore still has any standing toward the thief, which ties back to the argument between אביי and רבא.

the owners demanded from him, and he denied,

is the thief exempt through his admission to the guardian,

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a thief's admission to a שומר who swore exempts the thief from כפל when the owner later brings witnesses.

steps.title: רבא: It depends on whether the bailee's oath was true
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question from step 7. If the שומר swore truthfully, the thief's admission to him frees the thief from כפל. If the שומר swore falsely, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If the bailee's oath was true, the thief is exempt because he admitted to the bailee. If the bailee's oath was false, the thief is not exempt because of that admission.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question about the thief who admitted to the שומר and denied to the owner. His answer depends on whether the שומר's oath was honest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An admission only frees the thief from כפל if it is made to the right person, the one who has a claim. A שומר who swore truthfully is still a trusted שומר who can stand in for the owner, so admitting to him counts. A שומר who swore falsely has lost that trust, so admitting to him does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: swore truthfully
swore falsely
an admission made to the bailee

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רבא's follow-up question in steps 9-10, which asks exactly where the line is between an honest שומר and a dishonest one.

phrases.english: Rava says:

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא: אם באמת נשבע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A truthful oath keeps him a שומר, so the admission counts. A false oath means the admission does not count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether the thief is exempt depends on whether the שומר's oath was true.

steps.title: רבא asks about a bailee who was stopped before swearing falsely
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about a שומר who got up to swear falsely but was stopped. The question is left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: If the bailee got up to take a false oath but they did not let him, what is the law? The question stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tests the edge of his own ruling. Does a שומר who only tried to swear falsely lose his status, like one who actually swore falsely?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said a false oath disqualifies the שומר. Here no oath was actually taken, but he showed he was willing to lie. The גמרא cannot decide which matters more, so it ends with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: asked (a real question he could not settle)
they did not let him
the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: Rava asked:

and they did not let him, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a borderline case of the false-oath rule in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does only trying to swear falsely make the שומר lose his status?

steps.title: Another version of רבא's question: an actual false oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב כהנא taught רבא's question as above. רב טביומי taught that רבא asked about a שומר who actually swore falsely. That question is also unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא taught it this way. רב טביומי taught: רבא asked, if he swore falsely, what is the law? The question stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's question. In this version, רבא is unsure even about a שומר who really did swear falsely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב כהנא's version, a real false oath clearly disqualifies the שומר, and only the attempt is in doubt. In רב טביומי's version, the doubt is about an actual false oath. So in that version, it is not clear that a false oath takes away his status as a שומר.

steps.title: New question: the thief admits to the owners after the bailee paid
steps.stepSummary: The שומר paid the owners. The thief admitted to the owners but denied it to the שומר, who then brought witnesses. Does the admission to the owners free the thief from כפל?
steps.simpleTranslation: The owners demanded payment from the bailee and he paid. Then the thief was identified. The owners demanded from the thief and he admitted. The bailee demanded from him and he denied, and the bailee brought witnesses. Is the thief exempt because he admitted to the owners, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new case, the reverse of step 7. Now the thief admits to the owners and denies to the שומר. The next step will lay out the two ways of looking at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the שומר paid instead of swearing, so normally the right to the כפל moves to him. The question is whether the owners still count as a party, so that admitting to them frees the thief. If they have dropped out of the picture, admitting to them means nothing.

steps.title: The two sides of the question, left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the שומר can tell the owners they dropped out once they were paid. Or maybe the owners can say they did the שומר a favor by chasing the thief, so each side takes back its own. The question is left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say the bailee can tell the owners: "Since you took your money, you removed yourselves from this"? Or perhaps the owners can tell him: "Just as you did something for us, we also did something for you. We took the trouble to chase the thief. We take ours, and you take yours"? The question stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question in step 11 is hard by giving each side's argument. It cannot decide between them, so it ends with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: once the owners were paid, they are out, so admitting to them is like admitting to a stranger. Side two: the owners stayed involved by chasing the thief. They can take back their item, and the שומר takes back his money. If so, admitting to them may still count.

The new question in steps 11-12 also ends in תיקו: it is unclear whether paid owners are still involved enough that admitting to them frees the thief from כפל.

steps.title: אביי: A known thief, a שומר חנם may choose, a שומר שכר must go to court
steps.stepSummary: A deposited animal was stolen באונס and the thief was later identified. אביי rules that a שומר חנם may either take the thief to court or swear and be free. A שומר שכר must take the thief to court and cannot swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: If the animal was stolen in a way the שומר could not prevent, and the thief became known, אביי said: If he is an unpaid שומר, he can choose to take the thief to court, or he can choose to swear. If he is a paid שומר, he takes the thief to court and does not swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling by אביי about a theft באונס where the thief is later found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the thief to court means the שומר pays the owner himself and then collects from the thief. Swearing means the שומר frees himself, and the owner has to go after the thief. אביי gives this choice only to a שומר חנם. A שומר שכר has to handle the thief himself.

steps.title: רבא: Both kinds of שומר must take the thief to court
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי. He holds that a שומר חנם and a שומר שכר alike must take the thief to court, and neither can just swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Both this one and that one take the thief to court and do not swear.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposing view: there is no choice, even for a שומר חנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is only about the שומר חנם. אביי lets him swear his way out. רבא does not, so once the thief is known, every שומר has to deal with him.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every שומר must take the known thief to court. Swearing is not an option.

steps.title: Does רבא argue with רב הונא בר אבין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ruling that רב הונא בר אבין sent, which matches אביי exactly. Does רבא really disagree with it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say רבא argues with רב הונא בר אבין? For רב הונא בר אבין sent this ruling: If it was stolen by force and the thief became known, an unpaid שומר can choose to take the thief to court or to swear, and a paid שומר takes the thief to court and does not swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא with an earlier ruling that gives the שומר חנם a choice, just as אביי said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר אבין's ruling clearly lets a שומר חנם swear. That seems to go directly against רבא. The גמרא does not want רבא to be arguing with an accepted ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: "Shall we say he argues?" This raises a possible conflict.
He sent a ruling, usually by letter from ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא פְּלִיגָא אַדְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר אָבִין?
phrases.english: Shall we say he argues with רב הונא בר אבין?
For רב הונא בר אבין sent:
If it was stolen by force and the thief became known,
if he is an unpaid guardian,

phrases.aramaic: רָצָה עוֹשֶׂה עִמּוֹ דִּין, רָצָה נִשְׁבָּע;
phrases.english: if he wants he goes to court with the thief, if he wants he swears;
and if he is a paid guardian,
he goes to court with the thief and does not swear.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא פְּלִיגָא אַדְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a שומר חנם cannot swear
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא בר אבין explicitly lets the שומר חנם choose to swear.

steps.title: רבא: That ruling is about a שומר who already swore
steps.stepSummary: רבא could answer that רב הונא בר אבין is talking about a שומר who swore before the thief was found.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could say to you: What case are we dealing with here? A case where he had already sworn first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by putting רב הונא בר אבין's ruling into a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שומר swore before anyone knew who the thief was, his oath already stands. רבא only says a שומר cannot choose to swear once the thief is known. So the two rulings are about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: "What case are we dealing with here?" This narrows a ruling to a specific case.
He swore first, before the thief was found

phrases.english: רבא could say to you:
What case are we dealing with here?
Where he had already sworn first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רָבָא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא בר אבין lets a שומר swear even after the thief is known.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is talking about a שומר who swore before the thief was identified.

steps.title: But the ruling says "if he wants, he swears"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the ruling's own words offer swearing as a choice for the future. That doesn't fit a שומר who has already sworn.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he says, "if he wants he goes to court, if he wants he swears"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 16 using the exact words of the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "If he wants, he swears" sounds like the oath has not happened yet. That clashes with the claim that he already swore.

keyTerms.meaning: "But he says..." This points to wording that doesn't fit the answer.

phrases.english: But "if he wants he goes to court with him,
if he wants he swears" is what he says!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רָצָה עוֹשֶׂה עִמּוֹ דִּין רָצָה נִשְׁבָּע קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the case is one where he already swore
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording presents swearing as a future choice.

steps.title: Read it as: he may stand by his oath or go to court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ruling. The שומר חנם who already swore may stick with his oath, or he may choose to take the thief to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: If the unpaid שומר wants, he stands by his oath; if he wants, he takes the thief to court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the wording so that it fits רבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "He swears" really means "he keeps the oath he already took." So the ruling never lets a שומר start a new oath after the thief is known, and רבא does not argue with רב הונא בר אבין.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is what he means": a rereading of a statement
He stands by the oath he already took

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, once the thief is known, no שומר can start a new oath to free himself. Only a שומר who already swore may rely on that oath.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
if the unpaid guardian wants, he stands by his oath,
phrases.notes: He keeps the oath he took before the thief was found, and the owner goes after the thief.

phrases.english: if he wants, he goes to court with the thief.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: רָצָה שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם עוֹמֵד בִּשְׁבוּעָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "He swears" means taking a new oath.
steps.terutzMaskana: "He swears" means standing by an oath he already took.

steps.title: רבה זוטי: The thief returned the animal and it died through negligence
steps.stepSummary: רבה זוטי asks a new question. The animal was stolen באונס, the thief brought it back to the שומר's house, and then it died through the שומר's negligence. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה זוטי asked it like this: If it was stolen by force, and the thief returned it to the שומר's house, and it died through negligence, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new question about whether the שומר's duty comes back once the animal is returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally even a שומר חנם is liable for פשיעה. The theft באונס had freed him. Now the animal is back with him and he was negligent.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked the question this way
Returned
Negligence

phrases.english: רבה זוטי asked it like this:

phrases.aramaic: נִגְנְבָה בְּאוֹנֶס, וְהֶחְזִיר גַּנָּב בְּבֵית שׁוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: If it was stolen by force, and the thief returned it to the guardian's house,
and it died through negligence, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה זוּטֵי בָּעֵי לַהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the case of theft באונס from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the שומר liable for negligence after the stolen animal is returned to him?

steps.title: Did his duty end, or did it come back? Left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the theft ended his job as guardian for good. Or maybe returning the animal brought it back under his care. The question stays unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that once it was stolen by force, his guarding is finished? Or maybe, once it was returned, it came back into his guarding? Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets out the two sides of רבה זוטי's question and leaves it undecided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the אונס closed his guardianship for good, so he is free even after negligence. Side two: the animal's return restarted his duty, so he is liable for negligence. No answer is reached.

keyTerms.meaning: His guarding is finished
It came back into his guarding
Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבה זוטי's question is left open: does a שומר's duty come back when a stolen animal is returned to him?

phrases.english: Do we say: since it was stolen by force,
his guarding is finished,
or perhaps, since he returned it,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: it came back into his guarding? Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן: כֵּיוָן דְּנִגְנְבָה בְּאוֹנֶס כָּלְיָא לֵיהּ שְׁמִירָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out both sides of the question from step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the guardianship ended for good or came back when the animal was returned.

steps.title: The guardian who says 'it was lost' and swears falsely
steps.stepSummary: A שומר says the פקדון was lost and swears to it. If witnesses show he ate it, he pays only the קרן. If he admits on his own, he pays קרן, חומש, and brings an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The owner asks, 'Where is my deposit?' The guardian answers, 'It was lost.' The owner says, 'I make you swear,' and the guardian says 'Amen.' Then witnesses testify that he actually ate it. He pays the value of the item. If he admits by himself, he pays the value, adds a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Its first case is a שומר who falsely swears that the item was lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He claimed 'lost,' not 'stolen,' so the double payment does not apply. When witnesses catch him, he only returns the קרן. The extra חומש and the אשם come only when he admits on his own that his oath was false.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of a new משנה.
A deposit: an item left with a guardian for safekeeping.
'I make you swear.' The owner puts the guardian under oath.
The principal, meaning the basic value of the item.
An extra fifth added on top of the principal.
A guilt-offering brought for a false oath about money.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that getting caught by witnesses is always worse. In this case, the one who admits on his own pays more, the קרן plus חומש plus an אשם, than the one caught by witnesses, who pays just the קרן.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"Where is my deposit?"
He said to him: "It was lost."
"I make you swear," and he said "Amen,"
phrases.notes: Saying 'Amen' to an oath counts as swearing it yourself.

phrases.english: and the witnesses testify about him that he ate it —
he pays the principal.
[If he admitted on his own —
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets; the corrected wording adds them.

phrases.english: he pays the principal and a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.]

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ ״הֵיכָן פִּקְדוֹנִי?״ אָמַר לוֹ: ״אָבַד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous discussion ended with a תיקו. A new משנה begins here.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר who falsely swears 'it was lost' and is caught by witnesses pays קרן only. If he admits on his own, he pays קרן, חומש and brings an אשם.

steps.title: The guardian who says 'it was stolen' and swears falsely
steps.stepSummary: A שומר says the פקדון was stolen and swears to it. If witnesses show he stole it himself, he pays double. If he admits on his own, he pays קרן, חומש, and brings an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner asks, 'Where is my deposit?' The guardian answers, 'It was stolen.' The owner says, 'I make you swear,' and he says 'Amen.' Witnesses then testify that he stole it himself. He pays double. If he admits by himself, he pays the value, adds a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case that matches the first. Now the guardian's false claim is 'stolen' instead of 'lost.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blaming a thief and swearing falsely puts the guardian himself in the place of the thief, so witnesses obligate him in תשלומי כפל. If he admits by himself, there is no double payment. He pays the same as in the first case: קרן, חומש and an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was stolen.' This is the claim that a thief took it.
Double payment, the penalty a thief pays.
He admitted on his own, without witnesses.

steps.whyThisMatters: Put next to the first case, this shows that the double payment depends on the guardian's claim of 'stolen'. A claim of 'lost' does not bring it.

phrases.english: "Where is my deposit?"
He said to him: "It was stolen."
"I make you swear," and he said: "Amen,"
and the witnesses testify about him that he stole it —
he pays the double payment.
If he admitted on his own —
he pays the principal, a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הֵיכָן פִּקְדוֹנִי?״ אָמַר לוֹ: ״נִגְנַב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to step 21, with the claim changed from 'lost' to 'stolen'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר who falsely swears 'it was stolen' and is shown by witnesses to have stolen it pays תשלומי כפל. If he admits on his own, he pays קרן, חומש and brings an אשם.

steps.title: The son who robbed his father and swore falsely
steps.stepSummary: A son robs his father, swears falsely, and the father dies. The son pays קרן and חומש to his father's sons or brothers and brings an אשם. If he won't or can't pay, he borrows, and the creditors collect from his share.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone robs his father and swears to him falsely, and then the father dies. He pays the value plus a fifth to the father's sons or brothers, and brings a guilt-offering. If he does not want to, or does not have the money, he borrows, and the lenders come and collect payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case. A son must return what he robbed, but the person he robbed, his father, has died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the father's death, the stolen money belongs to his heirs, and the son is one of them. Even so, the משנה says he pays the other heirs, the father's sons or brothers, and does not simply keep the item as his own share. If he can't or won't pay out of pocket, he borrows the money, and his creditors are later repaid from his share.

keyTerms.meaning: One who robs his own father.
He borrows money.
Creditors, the people who lent him money.
They get repaid.

phrases.english: One who robs his father,
and swears to him, and he died —
phrases.notes: 'He died' means the father died, after the son swore falsely to him.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם קֶרֶן וָחוֹמֶשׁ וְאָשָׁם
phrases.english: this one pays the principal and a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering
to his sons or to his brothers.
phrases.notes: 'His' means the father's: the father's other sons, or the father's brothers.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה אוֹ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ –
phrases.english: And if he does not want to, or he does not have —
he borrows, and the creditors come and are repaid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַגּוֹזֵל אֶת אָבִיו, וְנִשְׁבַּע לוֹ, וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the משנה: returning stolen property when the robbery victim has died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son who robbed his father and swore falsely pays קרן and חומש to the father's other heirs and brings an אשם. If he cannot or will not pay, he borrows, and the creditors collect from his share.

steps.title: A father's vow forbidding his son, and the son still inherits
steps.stepSummary: A father forbids his son with a קונם from benefiting from his property. After the father dies, the son still inherits from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says to his son, 'קונם! You may not benefit from what is mine,' and then the father dies, the son inherits from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with one more case about a father's property. This time it is a vow forbidding the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow only forbade 'what is mine', meaning what belongs to the father. Once the father dies, the property is no longer his, so the vow no longer blocks the son, and he inherits normally.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow word that makes something forbidden like a קָרְבָּן (an offering).
Benefits from.
He will inherit from him.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rulings: 'Lost' plus witnesses means the קרן only. 'Stolen' plus witnesses means double. Admitting on your own means קרן, חומש and an אשם. A son who robbed his father pays the other heirs. A father's קונם against his son ends at the father's death, so the son inherits.

phrases.english: One who says to his son:
"Konam! You may not benefit from what is mine,"
if he dies — he inherits from him.
phrases.notes: The father is the one who dies, and the son is the one who inherits.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לִבְנוֹ: ״קוּנָּם אִי אַתָּה נֶהֱנֶה מִשֶּׁלִּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further case in the משנה, also about a father's property passing to his son after death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son forbidden by his father's קונם from benefiting from his property inherits him after his death.
